newsitem.title: USA: Clinton goes shopping, gets gift.
newsitem.headline: Clinton goes shopping, gets gift.

text.p: President Bill Clinton received an early Christmas gift on Tuesday when an Ethiopian immigrant gave him a compact disc and a compliment during a presidential shopping trip to a northern Virginia mall.
Eyassu Teklu said he went up the president, who was striding through clusters of last-minute holiday shoppers, and gave him the CD "Elemental Rhythm and Blues."

"I told him I was an Ethiopian and as an immigrant loved him very much," said the 38-year-old Teklu, an Alexandria, Virginia, resident who came to the United States 18 years ago and now runs a car dealership.
He said Clinton told him "We love having you here." But Teklu said he was disappointed none of the gaggle of photographers that trail Clinton snapped a shot of him shaking the president's hand.

The president shook off a press escort minutes after entering the Pentagon City Mall through a side door. His presence amazed and delighted shoppers, loaded down with bags and children, who followed him and his Secret Service escort as he examined goods in the windows of Scribner's bookstore, the Wentworth Gallery and other stores in the upscale shopping centre.

The president arrived at the mall in the early afternoon after playing nine holes of golf with his brother-in-law Tony Rodham at the Army Navy Country Club on a unusually mild December day that turned soggy when a steady rain began to fall.
